name: Research Stabilised → Transition to Dev-via-Spec
description: When the research-reviewer emits decide(action=approved), the research arc has stabilised — the reviewer's persona enforces the stabilisation predicate (reviewer-as-enumerator checklist passes AND the latest revision had no new substrate mutations) before approving. This rule fires on that signal and spawns the dev-via-spec planner specialist, transitioning the loop into dev-via-spec mode. R3.2.2 of the ADR-031 phasing introduced the persona-swap gate; R3.3 (ADR-031 §addendum 2026-04-30 'R3.3 dev-via-spec port') replaced the planner stub with the real four-role chain (planner / reviewer / challenger / architect). The dev-via-spec rules in configs/rules/dev-via-spec/ drive the chain forward; this rule is the entry point.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.dev-via-spec-plan
on_enter.prompt: Research has stabilised. The reviewer at loop $entity.instance approved the latest research artifact (reviewer-as-enumerator checklist passed AND zero new substrate mutations on the latest revision — see ADR-031 §addendum 2026-04-30 'Stabilisation as converged change-log' for the stabilisation predicate). Call read_loop_result with the reviewer loop id to load the artifact, then proceed per your persona's output contract.

metadata.stabilisation_predicate_location: research-reviewer persona (configs/personas/fragments/research-reviewer/15-stabilisation-check.md). The rule trusts the reviewer's decide(approved) gate per ADR-028 §Layer 2 (rules carry references not content; structured terminal output gates downstream rules deterministically).
metadata.defense_in_depth_gap: Rule trusts the reviewer's decide(approved). A real LLM reviewer mis-applying the gate (folding the stabilisation check into the checklist rather than firing it before) could bypass stabilisation. R3.3 should evaluate adding a defense-in-depth condition matching research.artifact.last_revision_mutation_count==0 — but that triple lives on the researcher's loop entity, not the reviewer's, so this requires cross-entity matching support in the rule expression engine (verify against beta.27+). Until then, the persona-fragment ordering (15-stabilisation-check.md before 20-osh-driver-checklist.md) keeps the eval order documented and visible.
